reproduction_target: Cell-type and developmental-epoch resolved genetic liability architecture of autism in SPARK. Computational target: (i) construction of 91 cortical cell-type x developmental-epoch gene sets from the Herring et al. developing prefrontal-cortex snRNAseq atlas (scanpy / AnnData / Scrublet QC, per-gene sensitivity-specificity-AUC, comparison of z-score / Wilcoxon / Expression Proportion / Expression Enrichment, fixed 600-gene sets, LOEUF filtering, PCA-AUC validation); (ii) SPARK genotype and exome processing (PLINK / KING QC, PennCNV + QuantiSNP + CNVision CNV calling via MIND-GENESPARALLELCNV, DigCNV machine-learning artefact filtering, GENCODE V19 annotation; GATK + DeepVariant short-variant intersection with VEP 113.3 / LoFtee / AlphaMissense / SpliceAI annotation through the Zenodo-deposited ShortVariants-Annotation Nextflow workflow); (iii) Functional Burden Association Tests (FunBAT) relating cell-type gene-set burden to ASD by conditional logistic regression across six variant classes, plus de novo enrichment, gene-set subsampling gene prioritisation, SKAT burden-vs-variance comparison, ASD-DEG comparison, and sex / age-at-diagnosis liability-bias permutation analyses. Saliva DNA extraction with GSA-24v1-0 genotyping and the SPARK iWESv3 exome sequencing are W (out of computational-reproduction scope).
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool/analysis, built from the bioRxiv v1 JATS XML (fetched with curl into an isolated per-paper scratch directory; the title phrase 'Cortical Cell-Type Liability Architecture of Autism' was confirmed present in the fetched XML before scoring) plus the prose of the four artefacts named under Code availability: github.com/JacquemontLab/FunBAT, github.com/JacquemontLab/DigCNV, github.com/JacquemontLab/MIND-GENESPARALLELCNV and the two Zenodo deposits (10.5281/zenodo.16268986 short-variant annotation workflow; 10.5281/zenodo.17860027 analysis notebooks). READMEs and Zenodo landing pages were read as prose only; no workflow source, notebook or nextflow.config was read at line level and nothing was executed. Data-axis convention used here: 2 = retrievable from this paper alone (open DOI or public resource named with a release), 1 = controlled access (SPARK individual-level data via SFARI Base application; derived measures 'upon request') or public-but-cited-only-by-literature-reference (the Herring et al. atlas is an open published resource but this paper states no accession, URL or download date). Version axis is capped at 1 throughout per the Stage-1 rule: the ShortVariants-Annotation workflow does claim Nextflow 25.10.2 plus four ghcr.io images, but those are ':latest' tags with no digest and the claim is unverified at prose level. NOTE: this record replaces an earlier draft written to the same path on 2026-07-28 09:35 by a prior run of the same Stage-1 task; the two agree on paper_type, capture_claim, stage2_candidate and the RI/NI split, and differ only in step granularity (17 vs 18 C-steps) and gap-dictionary usage.

steps.label: Wet-lab: saliva DNA extraction (OGD-500 kit, DNA Genotek) and SNP genotyping of SPARK participants on an Illumina GSA-24v1-0 array (654k SNP sites)
Wet-lab: exome sequencing of the SPARK iWESv3 cohort producing the per-individual gVCF files consumed by the short-variant pipeline (performed upstream by SPARK, cited to reference [21])

Download and quality control of the Herring et al. developing prefrontal-cortex snRNAseq atlas (154,748 nuclei, 26 donors, GW22-40y): scanpy (v1.6.0) and AnnData (v0.7.4) default filters plus the original-study filters - genes in <5 nuclei, Scrublet (v0.2.2) doublets, gene counts <3 MADs and <300 genes, ribosomal >20% / mitochondrial >3% per-sample MADs, MALAT1-high cells; restriction to 15,091 autosomal protein-coding genes of 26,747 detected; CPM scaling and log transform with the scanpy implementation

Reuse of the 18 author-defined cell-type labels (52 marker genes) and binning of donor age into 6 developmental epochs (prenatal, neonatal, infancy, childhood, adolescence, adult); removal of 1,275 author-flagged poor-quality cells and 153 cells in cell-type x epoch combinations with <50 cells, giving 153,325 cells and 91 cell-type x epoch units. No tool or version named

Per-gene sensitivity, specificity, ROC and AUC computation against each cell type (sensitivity = fraction of in-type cells with read count >=1; specificity = fraction of out-of-type cells not expressing the gene; SensitivityMax / SpecificityMax / AUCMax taken across cell types). Custom analysis; no library or version named

Cell-type gene-set construction: exclusion of 7,658 genes with sensitivityMax <10%, comparison of four assignment metrics (z-score, Wilcoxon via the scanpy implementation, Expression Proportion, Expression Enrichment), and selection of fixed 600-gene sets per cell type (~top 5% most specific autosomal genes); z-score adopted for all downstream gene sets

Validation of the gene sets: for each of the four specificity metrics, 15 windows of 100 genes (100th to 1,500th most specific) per cell type, PCA of their expression across the 153,325 cells, discrimination measured as the AUC of the first component; plus a bootstrap of 600 genes randomly sampled 500 times to test residual ASD liability among unassigned genes. No PCA implementation named, no RNG seed reported

Extraction of gene annotations: prenatal ('falling') and postnatal ('rising') brain-expressed gene lists from Werling et al.; LOEUF (oe.lof.upper) of the MANE transcript from gnomAD v4.1; ubiquitous and not-brain-expressed genes from the Human Protein Atlas. The manuscript records the HPA provenance literally as 'the HPA (date/version)' - an unfilled template placeholder

Definition of the 283 high-confidence ASD genes (hcASD) as the union of SFARI-Gene Release 2025 Q1 category-1 genes (n=232), Satterstrom et al. FDR<0.05 genes (n=102) and Fu et al. FDR<0.001 genes (n=72); broader definition at the gene-contribution step (all three SFARI categories plus syndromic genes, and Fu et al. FDR<0.05, n=185)

SPARK array QC and CNV calling: autosomal SNPs with MAF>5%, HWE p>1e-6, call rate >90%; PLINK (1.9) duplicate / sex / relatedness checks; ancestry PC1-10 with KING on 3,615 common SNPs against 1000 Genomes; PennCNV and QuantiSNP calling via github.com/JacquemontLab/MIND-GENESPARALLELCNV (>=3 consecutive probes, size >=1kb, likelihood >=15) merged with CNVision; array-level QC (call rate >=95%, LRR SD <0.35, BAF SD <0.08, |waviness| <0.05, <50 CNVs). Versions are given only for PLINK; KING, PennCNV, QuantiSNP, CNVision and the repository itself are unversioned (repo archived 2025-07-14, no releases)

CNV filtering and artefact removal: likelihood >=30, size >=50kb, <50% overlap with segmental duplications / HLA / centromeric regions; DigCNV machine-learning artefact detection (github.com/JacquemontLab/DigCNV, no version or release cited, pre-trained model described only by reference to Huguet et al.); GENCODE V19 (hg19) Ensembl gene annotation; cross-batch CNV frequency harmonisation over 4 SPARK batches by chi-square with FDR correction (n=36,360), excluding 2,135 heterogeneous CNVs

Short-variant (SNV/indel) QC and annotation from SPARK iWESv3 gVCFs: retention of variants called by both GATK and DeepVariant, DP>=20, GQ>=30, allele-balance 0.2-0.8; rarity filter MAF<1/1,000 against gnomAD v4.1 and within SPARK; Ensembl VEP release 113.3 on GRCh38 restricted to MANE transcripts; five consequence classes with LoFtee high-confidence for frameshift / stop-gained, AlphaMissense >=0.9 for missense and SpliceAI max delta >=0.8 for splice. Workflow deposited at Zenodo (JacquemontLab/ShortVariants-Annotation, tagged releases v1.0-v4.0, Nextflow 25.10.2, four ghcr.io images referenced by ':latest' tag with no digest)

Functional Burden Association Tests (FunBAT): per-gene per-individual collapsing of same-class variants into binary indicators, summation over the gene set (Formula 1), multigenic CNV correction by two complementary genome-wide burdens split at LOEUF=1 (Formula 2), and conditional logistic regression (statsmodels ConditionalLogit) with covariates sex, first 10 PLINK PCs and the individual's rare synonymous count; exclusion of 12,955 non-informative families (16,910 individuals). Code at github.com/JacquemontLab/FunBAT (no release or tag; README requires Python 3.8 or higher with unpinned pandas / numpy / scipy / statsmodels)

Sensitivity analyses on the burden results: recomputation across gene-specificity percentiles from the top 90th (~1,000 genes) to the top 99th (~100 genes), and cohort downsampling at nine family-sampling fractions (10%-90%, step 10%) repeated 20 times, with Spearman correlation of downsampled to original liabilities. No RNG seed reported

De novo variant analysis in 31,814 offspring from 20,130 families: de novo defined as absent from both parents at >=1 read regardless of variant QC, one variant per gene kept by strongest Ensembl consequence, removal of 28 individuals with >10 de novo synonymous genes; Fisher's exact enrichment of de novo variants across the 91 cell-type gene sets under two contingency-table constructions (de novo vs inherited inside/outside the gene set; ASD vs non-ASD sibling), restricted to constrained cortically expressed genes (LOEUF<0.6)

Gene-set subsampling for gene prioritisation: bootstrap version of FunBAT generating 1,000 sub-gene sets of 100 randomly sampled genes per cell type in the epochs significant after hcASD removal, recomputation of the ASD burden per sub-gene set (FDR<0.05, n=1,000) and prioritisation of genes enriched among the significant sub-gene sets (Fisher's exact test, FDR<0.05). The bootstrap driver is described as a variant of FunBAT; no seed and no separate release

Comparison of variance and burden approaches with the R package SKAT: SKAT-Variance vs SKAT-Burden applied to the collapsed per-gene information per variant class, corrected for sex and the first 10 principal components, significance at p=1e-4 (Bonferroni, n=364 tests). No SKAT package version, no R version and no driver script are cited for this step

ASD-DEG comparison: extraction of ASD differentially expressed genes for 36 cell types from Wamsley et al. at the authors' thresholds (FDR<0.05, log2FC>0.2), retention of the 47 sets with >100 DE genes, effect-size normalisation against 540 random gene sets (sizes 50-950 in steps of 50, 30 sets per size), recomputation of cell-type-specific gene sets from control-individual cells of the Wamsley expression matrix using the C1-C4 method, and burden testing across the six variant classes with correlation against the Herring-derived equivalents

Liability-bias analyses between ASD subgroups: recomputation of the 91 cell-type burdens within male vs female ASD and within early (<4y) vs late (>=4y) age at diagnosis, with a permutation test randomly splitting ASD individuals 5,000 times at the observed sex ratio (0.27 / 0.73), significance where the observed odds-ratio difference falls outside the 5th-95th percentile of the permutation distribution, empirical p-values FDR-corrected; plus a Mann-Whitney U comparison of male/female diagnosis age and sex-stratified de novo excess tests. No RNG seed reported

headline.static_readiness: 0/17 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification); unexecuted; declared environment statically valid but not verified as the env that produced the results. n_exact_capture_unexecuted=0, n_fetch_required=0.
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: RI ceiling on 7/17 computational steps (C1, C4, C6, C7, C8, C9, C10). These carry partial exact pins in prose - scanpy v1.6.0, AnnData v0.7.4, Scrublet v0.2.2, PLINK 1.9, VEP release 113.3, gnomAD v4.1, GENCODE V19 (hg19), SFARI-Gene Release 2025 Q1 - and, for C10 only, a Zenodo-archived tagged Nextflow workflow (JacquemontLab/ShortVariants-Annotation, tags v1.0-v4.0, nextflow 25.10.2, four ghcr.io images). Version stays at 1 for all of them because no environment closure is demonstrated at prose level: the container references are ':latest' tags with no digest, and no lockfile, conda environment or pinned requirements file is claimed anywhere. The remaining 10/17 steps cap at NI: C2, C3, C5, C11-C17. The dominant NI cause is the complete absence of version information for the software that produces the paper's headline results - the FunBAT package itself (no release or tag; README installs unpinned pandas / numpy / scipy / statsmodels on 'Python 3.8 or higher'), the R package SKAT and the R interpreter, the custom sensitivity-specificity-AUC and PCA code, and the bootstrap / permutation drivers. A secondary cause is stochasticity without seeds: the 500-fold gene bootstrap (C5), the 20-repeat family downsampling (C12), the 1,000 sub-gene-set bootstrap that yields the prioritised gene lists (C14) and the 5,000-fold permutation test that defines the sex and age-at-diagnosis bias significance (C17) are all reported without an RNG seed, so those results are reproducible only in distribution. Even under Stage-2 execution no step could exceed RI without an executed environment capture, because the strongest capture claimed anywhere in the record is a Zenodo release snapshot whose containers are referenced by mutable tag.
headline.coverage: 17 computational analysis steps assessed from the bioRxiv v1 JATS Methods plus the prose of the four Code-availability artefacts. 2 wet-lab steps (saliva DNA extraction with GSA-24v1-0 array genotyping; SPARK iWESv3 exome sequencing) counted in W and verdicted OOS, out of computational-reproduction scope. Coverage = 19/19 (100%) of enumerated steps.

gaps.missing: No environment lockfile, conda/mamba environment file, pinned requirements set, renv.lock or container image digest is claimed in the paper or in any of the four Code-availability artefacts. The strongest environment statement in the record is in the ShortVariants-Annotation README, which requires 'nextflow version 25.10.2' and pulls four images as 'docker://ghcr.io/jacquemontlab/ensembl_vep_113:latest', 'docker://ghcr.io/jacquemontlab/pyspark:latest', 'docker://ghcr.io/jacquemontlab/genomics_tools:latest' and 'docker://ghcr.io/jacquemontlab/duckdb_python:latest' - four mutable ':latest' tags with no digest. The FunBAT README states only 'Python 3.8 or higher' plus pandas, numpy, scipy and statsmodels installed with 'pip install -r requirements.txt', with no versions shown; DigCNV is installed as 'pip install digcnv' with no version; MIND-GENESPARALLELCNV documents no dependencies at all beyond 'The tools only work on linux64 for the moment'; the analysis-notebook deposit carries no environment file.
gaps.how_to_close: Replace the four ':latest' ghcr.io references with digest-pinned image references, publish a conda-lock or pip-compile lockfile covering the FunBAT and notebook stacks (pandas, numpy, scipy, statsmodels, scanpy, anndata, scrublet) and an renv.lock for the SKAT analysis, and cite these from Code availability.

gaps.where: Code availability - the four cited artefacts
gaps.missing: None of the three GitHub repositories carries a release or tag (FunBAT: releases[] empty, last push 2026-01-14; DigCNV: releases[] empty, last push 2025-09-11; MIND-GENESPARALLELCNV: archived 2025-07-14, releases[] empty, no licence), so the cited URLs float against a moving default branch. The analysis-notebook deposit (10.5281/zenodo.17860027, 'Analysis notebooks', scripts.zip, 20.7 MB, Python / Jupyter / R) is labelled development status 'Wip' and has no description, no README, no driver script and no mapping from notebook to figure. Consequently no identifiable published code exists for the sensitivity-specificity-AUC computation, the PCA-AUC validation, the SKAT comparison harness, the de novo enrichment or the permutation-based bias tests beyond whatever is inside that undocumented archive.
gaps.how_to_close: Tag a release on each of the three repositories and archive each to Zenodo with a versioned DOI cited from Code availability; add a README and a top-level driver to the notebooks archive mapping each notebook to the figure or table it produces, and lift its status out of 'Wip'.

gaps.where: Data availability - SPARK genotype, exome and phenotype data (steps C8-C17)
gaps.missing: SPARK genetic and phenotypic data are controlled access, obtainable only by application at https://base.sfari.org/, and the paper states that 'Derived measures at the individual level used in this study are available upon request (S.J., sebastien.jacquemont@umontreal.ca)'. Ten of seventeen computational steps therefore depend on data no reader can retrieve from the paper, and the exact SPARK release or freeze used (iWESv3 plus four array batches, 124k+ participants, 31,814 trios) is not identified by a versioned accession.
gaps.how_to_close: Cite the exact SPARK data release identifier and freeze date used, and deposit the derived individual-level measures under a controlled-access DOI with a documented request procedure rather than a personal email address.

gaps.where: Methods 'snRNAseq data' and 'Analysis of the ASD-DEG' - third-party expression datasets (steps C1-C6, C16)
gaps.missing: The snRNAseq atlas underlying every gene set in the paper is identified only by a literature reference ('we downloaded and used the 154,748 cells sampled from the prefrontal cortices of 26 individuals aged from gestational week 22 to 40 years old [1]'), with no accession, portal URL or download date. The Wamsley et al. ASD-DEG lists and expression matrix used in C16 are likewise cited only by reference with no accession or supplementary-table identifier.
gaps.how_to_close: State the accession (GEO / portal) and download date for the Herring et al. matrix and the exact supplementary-table identifier and accession for the Wamsley et al. DE gene lists and control-cell expression matrix.

gaps.missing: Four stochastic procedures are reported without an RNG seed or a published seeding scheme: the 600-gene bootstrap sampled 500 times (C5), the family downsampling at nine fractions repeated 20 times (C12), the 1,000 randomly sampled 100-gene sub-gene sets per cell type used for gene prioritisation (C14), and the 5,000-fold ASD-individual permutation test that defines significance for the sex and age-at-diagnosis liability biases (C17). The gene-prioritisation output (the microglia / L56_TLE4 / ID2 gene lists) and the sex-bias significance calls are therefore reproducible only in distribution, not exactly.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish the seed (or the seeded driver script) for each resampling procedure and release the realised sub-gene-set membership and permutation index tables alongside the summary statistics.

gaps.where: External resources consumed by the pipeline (steps C6, C7, C8, C9, C10)
gaps.missing: Pinning of external resources is uneven. gnomAD v4.1, VEP release 113.3, GENCODE V19 (hg19), GRCh38 and SFARI-Gene Release 2025 Q1 are pinned in prose. The Human Protein Atlas source is recorded literally as 'The ubiquitous and the not-brain-expressed genes were extracted from the HPA (date/version).' - an unfilled template placeholder that survived into the posted preprint, so neither the HPA release nor the download date is recoverable. The MANE transcript set, the 1000 Genomes reference panel used by KING, the LoFtee / AlphaMissense / SpliceAI resource versions, the DigCNV pre-trained artefact model, and the segmental-duplication / HLA / centromere region files used for CNV filtering are all cited without version or download date. Stage-1 cannot verify how any of these are fetched in code.
gaps.how_to_close: Fill in the HPA release and access date, and record release/version, download URL and checksum for MANE, 1000 Genomes, LoFtee, AlphaMissense, SpliceAI, the DigCNV model artefact and the CNV exclusion region files, fetched from pinned snapshots inside the workflow.

gaps.where: Code availability and Data availability - both Zenodo citations are concept DOIs
gaps.missing: Neither Zenodo DOI cited in the manuscript is version-specific; both resolve to whatever version is currently latest. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.16268986 (cited for short-variant QC and annotation, and repeated in Methods) now resolves to record 18607152, 'JacquemontLab/ShortVariants-Annotation: v4.0', published 2026-02-11 - two months after this preprint was posted on 2025-12-12 - whose release notes advertise 'New Nextflow workflows included' and 'Use of GitHub containers', i.e. an environment materially different from the v3.0-or-earlier the authors actually ran. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17822332 similarly resolves to record 17822333. A reader following the manuscript's citations therefore obtains code and data the paper did not use, with no indication of the substitution.
gaps.how_to_close: Cite version-specific Zenodo record DOIs for the exact releases used, and state the release tag alongside each DOI in Code availability and Data availability.

gaps.where: Steps C1, C4, C5 - method-selection decisions taken narratively
gaps.missing: Several consequential choices are justified in prose with no reproducible decision record: the sensitivityMax <10% cutoff that removes 7,658 genes, the fixed 600-gene set size ('about the top 5% most specific autosomal genes'), the choice of the z-score over Expression Enrichment on the basis of a bootstrap comparison whose code and outputs are not published, and the LOEUF<=0.6 exclusion applied 'unless stated otherwise'. Which figures and tables were produced under which variant is not stated per result.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish the parameter-sweep outputs behind each cutoff and annotate every figure with the gene-set size, specificity metric and LOEUF filter actually used.
